name: Faxian
summary: A Chinese monk in his sixties walks from Chang'an across the Taklamakan and Pamirs to the Buddhist holy land, then returns by sea via Sri Lanka and Java in search of complete Vinaya texts.

stops.note: Sets out with Huijing, Daozheng, Huiying and Huiwei to find complete Vinaya texts.
Keeps the summer retreat here and is joined by five more pilgrims.
Prefect Li Hao supplies the party before they enter the desert of drifting sands.
After seventeen days in the desert finds some four thousand Hinayana monks.
Poorly received, the party splits and Faxian's group turns south-west across the Taklamakan.
Watches the great procession of images in the fourth month at the Gomati monastery.
Spends some days here before climbing towards the Pamirs.
Keeps a retreat in the mountain kingdom before crossing the Congling range.
Sees a giant wooden image of Maitreya before descending the Indus gorges on rope ladders.
Keeps the summer retreat of 402 among some five hundred monasteries.
Visits Kanishka's great stupa and the Buddha's alms bowl.
Venerates the Buddha's skull-bone relic; Huijing later freezes to death crossing the Little Snowy Mountains.
Enters the Middle Kingdom and praises its mild government under the Guptas.
Visits the site of the Buddha's descent from the Trayastrimsa heaven.
Weeps at the ruined Jetavana monastery.
Finds the Buddha's birth city desolate, with few inhabitants.
Visits the site of the Buddha's parinirvana.
Sees the stupa where the Second Council was held.
Climbs Vulture Peak alone at night to recite the Surangama sutra.
Visits the tree under which the Buddha attained enlightenment.
Sees the Deer Park where the first sermon was preached.
Stays three years learning Sanskrit and copying the Mahasanghika Vinaya.
Spends two years copying sutras and drawing images at the Ganges mouth port.
After fourteen days at sea, stays two years in Sri Lanka and obtains more texts.
Storm-driven to an island where Brahmanism flourishes; waits five months for a ship.
Blown far off course, lands on the Shandong coast instead of Guangzhou.
Settles to translate texts with Buddhabhadra and writes his record.

sources.cite: Faxian, A Record of Buddhistic Kingdoms (Foguo ji), trans. James Legge, Oxford 1886
Max Deeg, Das Gaoseng-Faxian-Zhuan als religionsgeschichtliche Quelle, Wiesbaden 2005
